items.stem: Under what kind of tree does Siddhartha fall asleep?
items.quote: By the foot of the coconut tree, Siddhartha collapsed
items.why: He sleeps by the river.

items.stem: What colour is the monk's robe?
items.quote: a monk in a yellow robe with a shaven head
items.why: The robe marks a follower of the Buddha.

items.stem: When do the monks stop travelling?
items.quote: whenever it is not the rainy season, we always move from one place to another
items.why: They rest only in the rains.

items.stem: What did the place he fled smell of?
items.quote: there everything smelled of ointments, of spices, of wine
items.why: He remembers the rich life with distaste.

items.stem: Govinda gives him the greeting used for a gentleman before leaving.
items.quote: he gave him the salutation which one would use on a gentleman and went on his way
items.why: Govinda stays formal and polite.

items.stem: Siddhartha feels sad about starting over like a child.
items.quote: But he could not feel sad about this, no, he even felt a great urge to laugh
items.why: He wants to laugh, not cry.

items.stem: Complete: “he heard the water quietly ____”
items.quote: he heard the water quietly flowing
items.why: He wakes to a peaceful sound.

items.stem: Complete: “I know you, O Govinda, from your father’s ____”
items.quote: I know you, O Govinda, from your father’s hut
items.why: He recalls their shared past.

items.stem: Match each stage of his life to what filled it.
items.why: He looks back over his life.
evidence: As a boy, I had only to do with gods and offerings.
was searching for Brahman
But as a young man, I followed the penitents

items.stem: Put these events in story order.
items.why: Sleep leads to a meeting.

cards.text: He falls asleep under a tree
The monk goes on his way
He sees a monk sitting nearby

evidence: fell into a deep sleep
When he woke up after many hours
he saw a person sitting opposite to him
went on his way

items.stem: On waking, what does Siddhartha see above him?
items.quote: saw with astonishment that there were trees and the sky above him
items.why: He slowly remembers where he is.

items.stem: What does Govinda's face still express?
items.quote: expressed zeal, faithfulness, searching, timidness
items.why: His friend has aged but not changed.

items.stem: What does Siddhartha tell Govinda is not eternal?
items.quote: not eternal, anything but eternal are our garments and the style of our hair
items.why: Outward things change.

items.stem: As he says “Things are going downhill,” what else does he see going downhill?
items.quote: he also saw the river going downhill
items.why: He finds his own fate in the water.

items.stem: Govinda recognises him after Siddhartha names their shared past.
items.quote: “You’re Siddhartha,” Govinda exclaimed loudly. “Now, I’m recognising you
items.why: Their past brings recognition.

items.stem: Siddhartha claims to Govinda that he is a Samana again.
items.quote: But I haven’t said to you that I was a Samana.
items.why: He says only that he is on a pilgrimage.

items.stem: Complete: “How clean and beautiful is the air here, how good to ____!”
items.quote: How clean and beautiful is the air here, how good to breathe!
items.why: He feels free.

items.stem: Match each thing to how it seemed to him on waking.
items.why: Waking feels like a new start.
evidence: the past seemed to him as if it had been covered by a veil
his entire long sleep had been nothing but a long meditative recitation of Om
was looking at the world as a new man

items.stem: What does he now see had held him back as a Brahmin?
items.quote: Too much knowledge had held him back
items.why: Knowledge fed his pride.

items.stem: Put these parts of his life in order.
items.why: His path took long detours.
evidence: insight came towards me in the form of the great Buddha’s teachings
I went and learned the art of love with Kamala
learned trading with Kamaswami
to unlearn thinking again

items.stem: Why did Govinda stay behind from his group?
items.quote: I stayed behind from my group and sat with you
items.why: He wanted to keep the sleeper safe.

items.stem: Why does Siddhartha stop at the river bank?
items.quote: Tiredness and hunger had weakened him
items.why: He is worn out.

items.stem: Why did he have to go out into the world, per ¶48?
items.quote: until the priest and Samana in him was dead
items.why: Only the world could end his pride.

items.stem: Why are the monks always travelling?
items.quote: live according to the rules of the teachings passed on to us
items.why: Their way of life requires it.

items.stem: Siddhartha still loves Govinda as he watches him leave.
items.quote: he loved him still, this faithful man
items.why: His affection lasts.

items.stem: Siddhartha says he needed a guard for his sleep.
items.quote: though I wouldn’t have required any guard
items.why: He thanks Govinda but needed no guard.

items.stem: Complete: “That lust for the world and riches do not belong to the good things, I have already learned as a ____.”
items.quote: That lust for the world and riches do not belong to the good things, I have already learned as a child.
items.why: He knew it early but lived it only now.

items.stem: Complete: “so full of trust, so without ____”
items.quote: so full of trust, so without fear
items.why: He feels like a child again.

items.stem: Match each cause to its result.
items.why: Each moment leads to an action.
evidence: with doubt in his eyes. After that, he gave him the salutation
thus refreshed, thus renewed, thus rejuvenated
Thinking was hard on him, he did not really feel like it, but he forced himself.

items.stem: Order his questions to his heart in ¶44.
items.why: He searches for the source of his joy.

cards.text: Did the word Om bring it?
Did the long sleep bring it?

evidence: Might it come from that long, good sleep
Or from the word Om, which I said?
Or from the fact that I have escaped
I praise you, Siddhartha

items.stem: Complete: “for much longer he could have lived in this soft, well upholstered ____”
items.quote: for much longer he could have lived in this soft, well upholstered hell
items.why: Comfort is pictured as torment.

items.stem: “like a sponge sucks up water until it is full” suggests what?
items.quote: like a sponge sucks up water until it is full
items.why: He has absorbed all he can bear.

items.stem: Calling his past life “a very old, previous incarnation” suggests what?
items.quote: this past life seemed to him like a very old, previous incarnation
items.why: The old life feels far behind.

items.stem: “Siddhartha the lustful, Siddhartha the greedy could also die” stresses what?
items.quote: until Siddhartha the lustful, Siddhartha the greedy could also die
items.why: Each role had to end.

items.stem: “Where is Siddhartha the Brahmin? … the rich man?” suggests what?
items.quote: Where is Siddhartha the Brahmin? Where is Siddhartha the Samana? Where is Siddhartha the rich man?
items.why: No role lasts.

items.stem: “now I’m starting again at the beginning and as a child” frames his loss as what?
items.quote: now I’m starting again at the beginning and as a child!
items.why: Loss becomes a new start.

items.stem: The list “in my eyes, in my heart, in my stomach” stresses what?
items.quote: don’t just know it in my memory, but in my eyes, in my heart, in my stomach
items.why: He knows it through experience.

items.stem: The river seeming to have “something special to tell him” hints at lessons still to come.
items.quote: It seemed to him as if the river had something special to tell him
items.why: The river will matter later.

items.stem: Siddhartha wakes feeling he has become a stranger to himself.
items.quote: But no, he knew himself, he knew his hand and his feet
items.why: He knows himself, though renewed.

items.stem: Order the steps of his reasoning in ¶45.
items.why: He sees why the crisis was good.

cards.text: He could have stayed with Kamaswami

evidence: he could have stayed with Kamaswami
the moment of complete hopelessness and despair
that he had not succumbed to it
this was why he laughed
